title: The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF Is Near Its All-Time High: Is It Still a Good Buy?
author: David Jagielski, Cpa
description: The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) has surged 22% this year and hit an all-time high, prompting questions about valuation. Despite the gains, the ETF maintains a reasonable price-to-earnings multiple of less than 20 (below the S&P 500's 23) and offers a 3% dividend yield, making it still attractive for income-focused investors seeking safety and quality dividend stocks.

Despite reaching all-time highs, the article concludes it remains an excellent buy for income-focused investors seeking safe, high-yielding dividend payments.

title: Wall Street Analysts Think Merck (MRK) Is a Good Investment: Is It?
author: Na
description: The article compares brokerage analyst recommendations (ABR) with Zacks Rank as investment decision tools. While Merck has a favorable average brokerage recommendation of 1.67 (Buy-equivalent), the article cautions that brokerage firms often exhibit positive bias due to vested interests. Zacks Rank, based on earnings estimate revisions rather than analyst opinions, is presented as a more reliable predictor of near-term stock price movements. Merck received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) due to unchanged earnings estimates, suggesting caution despite the bullish brokerage consensus.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Merck has a favorable average brokerage recommendation of 1.67 (Buy-equivalent with 62.1% Strong Buy ratings), the article advises caution. The company's unchanged consensus earnings estimate of $2.97 for the current year resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting the stock should perform in line with the broader market in the near term rather than outperform.

title: Should You Invest $1,000 in SCHD Right Now?
author: David Dierking
description: The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) has surged 22.8% year-to-date in 2026, outperforming the S&P 500's 11.8% gain. The rotation toward value and dividend stocks is expected to continue due to inflation concerns, higher interest rates, strong corporate earnings growth, and shrinking valuations. The ETF's focus on high-quality dividend-paying stocks positions it well for further gains.

title: AZN vs. MRK: Comparing Keytruda, Pipelines and Growth Strategies
author: Na
description: AstraZeneca and Merck are compared as investment opportunities in the pharmaceutical sector. AstraZeneca targets $80 billion in revenues by 2030 with 20 planned new medicine launches but faces patent expirations, pricing pressures in China, and recent pipeline setbacks. Merck relies heavily on blockbuster drug Keytruda (peak sales $35 billion by 2028) but faces patent expiration in 2028 and biosimilar competition. Merck receives a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) while AstraZeneca receives Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), making Merck the preferred choice despite higher valuation multiples.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock declined 9.7% year-to-date, facing multiple headwinds including patent expirations on mature drugs (Brilinta, Pulmicort, Soliris), sharp revenue declines from generic Farxiga, China market uncertainty, and recent clinical pipeline setbacks. Earnings estimates have been revised downward over the past 60 days. Assigned Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell).

Stock has risen 39.5% year-to-date with strong revenue growth driven by blockbuster Keytruda expected to maintain strong sales through 2028. Company has expanded pipeline with 20 planned drug launches by 2030, recent positive phase III data for personalized cancer therapy with Moderna, and strategic acquisitions to prepare for post-Keytruda period. Assigned Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), making it the preferred choice over AstraZeneca.

title: Wall Street's Bull Case for Bristol Myers Squibb Is Getting Louder
author: James Halley
description: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) is up 17% this year and trades at a discount to peers despite strong Q2 performance with $12.9B revenue and 153% EPS growth. The company's growth portfolio of newer drugs now accounts for nearly 60% of revenue and grew 15% year-over-year, offsetting concerns about patent expirations on legacy drugs. With a 3.95% dividend yield, $5B buyback program, and potential acquisition interest from AstraZeneca, analysts see significant upside potential as the market has underpriced the stock relative to its pipeline execution.
